Kevin L.: quick check — how should SDKs handle 429 + Retry-After for streaming responses? We saw a customer report where a 429 comes mid-stream (partial tokens already delivered). Do we try to resume, or surface an error and require a fresh request? cc @Maria G.

Maria G.: if you have a server-side resume token definitely try resume. For true streaming (no resume token) treat it like a transient failure: backoff + retry from the client, but only if the operation is idempotent or the server guarantees replay semantics. Otherwise surface an error. Also honor Retry-After if present. :white_check_mark:

Alex P.: TL;DR: implement exp-backoff with jitter, but prefer Retry-After when provided. For streams we do incremental retry windows and a small max attempts (3). Example pseudo-code for node client: 

```js
async function handleError(resp) {
  const status = resp.status;
  const retryAfter = parseRetryAfter(resp.headers['retry-after']); // seconds or date
  if (status === 429 || status >= 500) {
    if (retryAfter) await sleep(retryAfter * 1000);
    else await sleep(expBackoffWithJitter(attempt));
    return true; // try again
  }
  return false; // surface error
}
```

Alex P.: for streaming, when mid-stream 429 happens we: 1) try server resume token if provided, 2) otherwise attempt full retry only for idempotent calls (or when client included an Idempotency-Key). If neither, fail fast.

Sophia R.: a few gotchas: 1) Retry-After can be an HTTP-date — parse both. 2) For long-running streams, make retry windows adapt (don't retry too aggressively). 3) Idempotency-Key should be used for non-idempotent operations where clients expect safe retries (uploads, transforms). Server should return the same result if the key matches.

Sophia R.: snippet for headers we recommend: 

```
Idempotency-Key: <uuid>
Prefer-Resume: true
Resume-Token: <token>  // server-provided on first partial stream
```

Kevin L.: good call. For Ruby client does anyone have a small example of parsing Retry-After HTTP-date?

Alex P.: Ruby: 

```rb
if resp['retry-after']
  begin
    secs = Integer(resp['retry-after'])
  rescue ArgumentError
    secs = Time.httpdate(resp['retry-after']) - Time.now
  end
  sleep [secs, 0].max
end
```

Maria G.: also add a metric/trace for "stream_retry_attempt" and include the reason (429/5xx/retry-after) so we can tune limits.

ci-bot: docs: https://redwood.com/docs/clients/retries (internal)

Kevin L.: thanks all — I'll update the node + ruby SDK PR with these patterns, add tests for Retry-After date parsing and a small integration test that simulates mid-stream 429 + resume-token. pinging @Alex P. for review when ready.
